The resolvent cubic does have an exact root $k=-61$, since $2(-61)^3 + 121(-61)^2 - 8410(-61) - 509289 = 0$. Then $2k+121 = -1$, and the Ferrari setup becomes
$$(y^2-61)^2 = -(y+22)^2 \implies y^2 - 61 = \pm i(y+22).$$
Taking the $+$ sign gives $y^2 - iy - (61+22i) = 0$, so
$$y = \frac{i + \sqrt{243+88i}}{2}.$$
I checked this directly: $y^2 - iy = 61 + 22i$.

Shifting back, $x = y - 5 = \frac12\left(-10 + i + \sqrt{243+88i}\right)$. Numerically, $x \approx 2.92 + 1.89i$, which lies in the first quadrant. So $a=-10$, $b=1$, $c=243$, $d=88$, and
$$a+b+c+d = 322.$$

The proposed answer of 38 is incorrect.
